207	\label{app:advbench_layer_bias}

Because balanced accuracy, precision, and FPR share the same confusion matrix, the three per-model metrics are correlated; the effective number of independent comparisons is four (one per model). 28	Our contributions are:
29	\begin{itemize}
30	    \item \textbf{Metric-induced layer selection bias.} Prior work has noted metric sensitivity in probing~\citep{belinkov2022probing}; our contribution is demonstrating a qualitative reversal (significant to non-significant) in a safety-critical application, where the stakes of metric choice are higher than in typical linguistic probing. Crossing-rate composite metrics systematically select shallow layers across all four models (including Llama) and across datasets (HarmThoughts step-level CP labels and AdvBench binary jailbreak classification; \cref{app:advbench_layer_bias}), reversing HS probe conclusions at 32B scale. The divergence is not gradual: for QwQ-32B, the CR-composite layer (L2, 3\% depth) yields $p{=}0.83$ (non-significant), while the threshold-based layer (L63, 98\% depth) yields $p{<}0.005$, a qualitative reversal, not a quantitative shift. Random-label controls on both architectures confirm the disagreement requires genuine safety labels; the geometric component is Qwen-specific (\cref{sec:layer-results}).
31	
32	    \item \textbf{Boundary conditions for the HS advantage.} Against 384d MiniLM, the HS advantage is validated via nested 5-fold CV at 7--8B (+20.1 to +21.9pp, HB corrected), significant at QwQ-32B$^\dagger$ (+19.2pp, position-competitive), and exploratory at R1-32B$^\dagger$ (+15.4pp). This advantage is conditional on two partially correlated factors: it diminishes with stronger encoders (1/4 HB under BGE-1024d; PCA capacity matching preserves significance across all four models) and partially overlaps with position (3/4 linear, 2/4 quadratic residualization; \cref{sec:32b-analysis}).
33	
34	    \item \textbf{Negative results define method boundaries.} No alternative method consistently matches supervised probing (\cref{tab:negative}): BOCPD/CUSUM fail on gradual transitions; Mahalanobis distance finds near-zero separation; RepE is model-dependent; cross-model transfer fails. Control task selectivity (11.1--16.8pp above chance; \cref{app:control}) confirms genuine safety structure.
35	\end{itemize}
36	
37	\noindent These findings establish that layer selection metric is an uncontrolled confound in hidden-state safety probing: any study reporting conclusions from a single metric family risks undetected qualitative reversal.\looseness=-1

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Reasoning models such as DeepSeek-R1~\cite{deepseekr1} and QwQ~\cite{qwq} scale inference-time computation through extended chains of thought (CoT). Recent work documents that these models can ``self-jailbreak'': without adversarial input modification, the CoT transitions from safety-aware deliberation to committed harmful generation~\cite{harmthoughts,selfjailbreak}. We define the first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases as the \textbf{Safety Commitment Point} (CP). This failure mode differs qualitatively from adversarial jailbreaks on standard LLMs because the harmful transition originates within the model's own reasoning. Recent work shows that chain-of-thought faithfulness is limited~\citep{chen2025unfaithful}, motivating hidden-state monitoring that bypasses surface text. Before retrospective characterization can inform future detection systems, a prior question must be answered: can current probing methods reliably distinguish pre-CP from post-CP reasoning steps, and under what conditions? This paper provides \emph{retrospective} classification (not online detection) of what hidden-state and text-based probes can and cannot detect; false positive rates remain 11--50\%, so deployment applications are future work.\looseness=-1

Existing safety detectors target fundamentally different problems. Hidden-state (HS) methods such as TrajGuard~\cite{trajguard} and SafeSwitch~\cite{safeswitch} classify adversarial inputs at the token level, while text monitors like SafeRemind~\cite{saferemind} scan generated reasoning for explicit violations. Neither tracks the gradual, multi-step commitment process. HS probes require choosing which transformer layer to monitor, a researcher degree of freedom typically treated as a minor implementation detail. Before asking which modality is better, a prior methodological question must be answered: how sensitive are probe conclusions to the choice of layer selection metric? We show this choice alone can reverse a study's central conclusion: the same data yield a 14-layer (R1-8B) to 61-layer (QwQ-32B) divergence depending solely on metric choice; for QwQ-32B, at threshold-based layers the HS advantage is +19pp ($p{<}0.005$); at crossing-rate-selected layers, it is non-significant ($p{=}0.83$). Prior hidden-state probing targets standard LLMs~\citep{zhou2024alignment,arditi2024refusal}; prior reasoning safety work remains at the text level~\citep{harmthoughts,safethink}. The intersection---hidden-state monitoring of reasoning model safety trajectories---is unexplored, and existing hidden-state analyses operate across layers (spatial) rather than across generation steps (temporal).\looseness=-1

We conduct a systematic analysis across four reasoning models, primarily Qwen-based (3/4 models), with one Llama model providing evidence from a second architecture family, at two scales (7--8B, 32B) on the HarmThoughts benchmark. Our central finding is methodological: the choice of layer selection metric entirely determines whether an HS advantage is observed. A composite metric (balanced accuracy $\times$ crossing rate) selects shallow layers for 32B models because shallow representations compress directional information, so a linear probe operates near the noise floor and threshold crossings reflect noise rather than semantic transitions. At these layers, only the two 7--8B models show significant HS advantage.\looseness=-1

Data: HarmThoughts~\citep{harmthoughts} with step-level CP annotations (CP = first reasoning step after which safety deliberation permanently ceases). Split: 60/20/20.}
\label{tab:models}
\end{table}

Threshold-based metrics (precision, inverse FPR, additive composite) share a common confusion matrix and empirically converge; BA independently confirms deep-layer selection (\cref{tab:layer_selection}). At these layers, the HS advantage is graded: \emph{validated via nested 5-fold CV} at 7--8B (precision +20.1 to +21.9pp; \cref{tab:hs_vs_text}), \emph{significant} but suggestive of position-competitiveness at QwQ-32B$^\dagger$ (+19.2pp; \cref{sec:32b-analysis}), and \emph{exploratory} at R1-32B$^\dagger$ (+15.4pp, pattern consistent with position mediation, below MDE; \cref{sec:experiments}).\looseness=-1

Our contributions are:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Metric-induced layer selection bias.} Prior work has noted metric sensitivity in probing~\citep{belinkov2022probing}; our contribution is demonstrating a qualitative reversal (significant to non-significant) in a safety-critical application, where the stakes of metric choice are higher than in typical linguistic probing. Crossing-rate composite metrics systematically select shallow layers across all four models (including Llama) and across datasets (HarmThoughts step-level CP labels and AdvBench binary jailbreak classification; \cref{app:advbench_layer_bias}), reversing HS probe conclusions at 32B scale. The divergence is not gradual: for QwQ-32B, the CR-composite layer (L2, 3\% depth) yields $p{=}0.83$ (non-significant), while the threshold-based layer (L63, 98\% depth) yields $p{<}0.005$, a qualitative reversal, not a quantitative shift. Random-label controls on both architectures confirm the disagreement requires genuine safety labels; the geometric component is Qwen-specific (\cref{sec:layer-results}).

    \item \textbf{Boundary conditions for the HS advantage.} Against 384d MiniLM, the HS advantage is validated via nested 5-fold CV at 7--8B (+20.1 to +21.9pp, HB corrected), significant at QwQ-32B$^\dagger$ (+19.2pp, position-competitive), and exploratory at R1-32B$^\dagger$ (+15.4pp). This advantage is conditional on two partially correlated factors: it diminishes with stronger encoders (1/4 HB under BGE-1024d; PCA capacity matching preserves significance across all four models) and partially overlaps with position (3/4 linear, 2/4 quadratic residualization; \cref{sec:32b-analysis}).

    \item \textbf{Negative results define method boundaries.} No alternative method consistently matches supervised probing (\cref{tab:negative}): BOCPD/CUSUM fail on gradual transitions; Mahalanobis distance finds near-zero separation; RepE is model-dependent; cross-model transfer fails. Control task selectivity (11.1--16.8pp above chance; \cref{app:control}) confirms genuine safety structure.
\end{itemize}

\noindent These findings establish that layer selection metric is an uncontrolled confound in hidden-state safety probing: any study reporting conclusions from a single metric family risks undetected qualitative reversal.\looseness=-1
